newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat futures extend gains in closing rally.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat futures extend gains in closing rally.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed higher, extending their gains in a late short-covering surge, traders said.

KCBT wheat futures opened higher on bullish news in the USDA's weekly export report. Wheat held to the gains at the midsession after the EU announced wheat export refunds that came in at the low end of traders' expectations.
The EU said Thursday it granted 350,500 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a refund of 22.35 ECUs per tonne. Traders had expected a refund of between 23 and 25 ECUs.

Wheat was supported throughout the session by signs that the market was oversold technically in the short-term. Traders also said KCBT wheat was drawing support from a continued tight domestic supply of HRW wheat.

"Kansas City is still a domestic-driven beast. I think we gained here on the realization that (Wednesday's) CCC catalog sales won't break basis levels as much as people would have hoped," a trader said.

Traders said Wolcott Lincoln bought at least 1.5 million July bushels. FIMAT bought 1.3 million March and bull-spread 500,000 Dec/March bushels at 23 cents. Prudential bear-spread one million March/Dec bushels at 23 to 24 cents.
The Dec/March spread widened to trade at 24 cents late, after trading at 21 cents early.
Traders said commission houses were late buyers of KCBT Dec in technical-type short-covering.
